sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Configure maximum Pods per node (GKE)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: with the default of 110 Pods 'Kubernetes assigns a /24 CIDR block (256 addresses) to each of the nodes'; the block holds at least twice the maximum Pods; the worked example: 110 Pods per node and a /21 Pod range give 2^(24-21) = 8 nodes; maximum Pods per node 'cannot' be changed after the cluster or node pool is created, but a new node pool can set its own; when Pod addresses run out, 'you can create additional Pod IP address ranges using discontiguous multi-Pod CIDR'. The gcloud flags (--add-secondary-ranges, --pod-ipv4-range) are from memory of the CLI reference (to verify).

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Troubleshoot VPC-native clusters (GKE)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: the error '[IP_SPACE_EXHAUSTED] Instance ... creation failed: IP space of ... is exhausted'; each node reserves a contiguous block from the cluster's Pod range even if few Pods run; if the name in the error is [SUBNET_NAME]-[SECONDARY_RANGE_NAME]-[HASH] the Pod range is exhausted, if it is only the subnet name the node range is; remedies: add Pod IPv4 ranges (discontiguous multi-Pod CIDR) without re-creating the cluster, expand the subnet's primary range with expand-ip-range when nodes run out, or create a node pool with a smaller maximum Pods per node (110 reserves a /24, 32 a /26).

brief.situation: You are the network engineer for Orchard Lane Media, a fictional streaming site on Google Cloud. The GKE Standard cluster prod-web in us-central1 runs on subnet gke-prod. A promotion goes live at 12:00 and the web tier is scaling out for it: 40 Pods are Pending and the cluster autoscaler cannot add nodes.
handover: The cluster was built two years ago from a template; nobody has changed its ranges since.
There are 8 nodes today; capacity planning wants 14 for the promotion.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the subnet's primary range, the Pod ranges and the node pools.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The promotion goes live at 12:00, 55 minutes after the alert.

parts.label: Which
parts.criteria: Reads the error's range name and does the per-node arithmetic.
parts.modelAnswer: The IP_SPACE_EXHAUSTED message named gke-prod-pods-..., the Pod range; at 110 Pods per node each node reserves a /24, and a /21 holds 8, all used. The node range had 1,000 free addresses.

parts.label: Added
parts.criteria: Adds Pod address space without rebuilding the cluster.
parts.modelAnswer: Added secondary range pods-2 (10.14.0.0/21, checked against the address plan) and a node pool on it with 32 Pods per node, a /26 each, room for 32 nodes; the cluster kept running.

parts.label: Next time
parts.criteria: Plans capacity in node blocks, not Pods.
parts.modelAnswer: Capacity is node blocks: Pod range size divided by the per-node block. Size Pod ranges and max Pods per node for the largest node count, watch the IP utilization insight, and keep free space in the plan for more ranges.

rebuilt.headline: A bigger range, and an outage
rebuilt.body: A cluster does not need rebuilding to get more Pod addresses. Discontiguous multi-Pod CIDR adds a secondary range and a node pool that uses it while everything keeps running.

promoMissed.headline: The scale-out never happened
promoMissed.body: The error named the Pod range. Expanding the node subnet or retrying the old pool changes nothing; a new range and a pool that draws from it do.

scaled.headline: Good: the right range, no rebuild
scaled.body: You read which range the error named, worked out the per-node blocks, checked the new range against the plan, and added it with a pool that uses smaller blocks, then confirmed the Pods ran.

gaps.headline: Scaled, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: reading the error and the cluster, checking the new range against the plan, verifying, or a node range expanded for nothing.

scoring.modelReasoning: The scale-up failed with IP_SPACE_EXHAUSTED, and the name in the error is the subnet plus a secondary range, so the Pod range ran out, not the node addresses. At 110 Pods per node every node reserves a /24 from the Pod range; a /21 has room for exactly 8, and 8 nodes exist. Maximum Pods per node cannot be changed on an existing pool, and expanding the node subnet does nothing for Pods while being irreversible. Add a second Pod range from free address space and create a node pool on it with a smaller per-node block (32 Pods, a /26, 32 nodes in a /21); the cluster keeps running, unlike a rebuild. Verify the Pods schedule before 12:00 and plan Pod ranges in node blocks.
